displayedInputs.question: In a Cartesian coordinate plane, \(A(0,0)\), \(B(3,1)\), and \(C(1,-3)\). First use the converse of the Pythagorean theorem to determine the type of \(\triangle ABC\), then find its area (enter only the area).
How can you construct the point representing \(\sqrt{5}\) on the number line? (Choose the correct construction.)

choices.A: Construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 2 and 1. Draw an arc centered at the origin with radius equal to the hypotenuse length to intersect the positive half of the number line.
choices.B: Construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 1 and 1. Draw an arc centered at the origin with radius equal to the hypotenuse length to intersect the positive half of the number line.
choices.C: Construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 2 and 3. Draw an arc centered at the origin with radius equal to the hypotenuse length to intersect the positive half of the number line.

displayedInputs.question: To construct a point representing an irrational number on the number line, construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 1 and 3. Draw an arc centered at the origin with radius equal to the hypotenuse length, intersecting the positive half of the number line at point \(P\). What is the square of \(OP\)?

On the number line, point \(O\) represents 0 and point \(A\) represents 3. Draw a line through \(A\) perpendicular to the number line, and choose point \(B\) on this line such that \(AB=2\). Draw an arc centered at \(O\) with radius \(OB\), intersecting the positive half of the number line at point \(P\). Between which two consecutive integers does the number represented by \(P\) lie?

Point \(A\) on the number line represents \(-2\). Construct a right triangle with legs of lengths 1 and 3. Draw an arc centered at \(A\) with radius equal to the hypotenuse length, intersecting the number line to the right at point \(P\). Approximately what number does \(P\) represent? (Round to 1 decimal place.)
How many diagonals does an octagon have in total? (Enter only the number.)
How many diagonals can be drawn from one vertex of a decagon?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: A polygon with all sides equal is a regular polygon.
choices.B: A polygon with all angles equal is a regular polygon.
choices.C: A polygon with all sides equal and all angles equal is a regular polygon.
choices.D: From one vertex of an \(n\)-gon, \(n-2\) diagonals can be drawn.

displayedInputs.question: A total of 7 diagonals can be drawn from one vertex of a polygon. How many diagonals does this polygon have in total?
What is the sum of the interior angles of an octagon? (Unit: degrees; enter only the number.)
What is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon, in degrees? (Enter only the number.)
If all diagonals from one vertex of an \(n\)-gon are drawn, into how many triangles is it divided?
The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is \(1440^\circ\). How many sides does it have? (Enter only the number.)
The sum of all but one of the interior angles of a convex polygon is \(1300^\circ\). Find the measure of the omitted interior angle. (Unit: degrees.)
What is the measure of one exterior angle of a regular hexagon, in degrees? (Enter only the number.)
The sum of the exterior angles of any polygon (taking one exterior angle at each vertex) equals:

choices.D: Depends on the number of sides \(n\)

displayedInputs.question: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is \(150^\circ\). How many sides does it have? (Enter only the number.)
The sum of the interior angles of a polygon is 3 times the sum of its exterior angles. Find the number of sides of this polygon.
In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=70^\circ\). Find \(\angle B\). Also, \(AB=3\). Find \(CD\). (Answer in order, separated by a comma, without units.)
In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(\angle A=65^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle C\), in degrees. (Enter only the number.)
Which of the following properties does a parallelogram not necessarily have?

choices.A: Opposite sides are parallel and equal.

displayedInputs.question: The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) of parallelogram \(ABCD\) intersect at point \(O\). Given \(AC=10\), \(BD=14\), and \(AB=6\), find the perimeter of \(\triangle OAB\).
In parallelogram \(ABCD\), \(AB=5\) and \(BC=8\). The bisector \(AE\) of \(\angle BAD\) intersects side \(BC\) at point \(E\). Find the length of \(EC\).
If one pair of opposite sides of a quadrilateral is parallel and equal, is the quadrilateral a parallelogram?
Which of the following conditions is insufficient to conclude that quadrilateral \(ABCD\) is a parallelogram?
In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB\parallel CD\), \(AB=2x+1\), and \(CD=3x-4\) (unit: cm). What value must \(x\) take for quadrilateral \(ABCD\) to be a parallelogram?
In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), which of the following ratios \(\angle A:\angle B:\angle C:\angle D\) establishes that it is a parallelogram?
In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB\parallel CD\), \(AB=CD=7\), and \(BC=4\). Find the perimeter of quadrilateral \(ABCD\).
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) and \(E\) are the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively. If \(BC=10\), how long is \(DE\)? (Enter only the length of \(DE\).)
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(D\) and \(E\) are the midpoints of \(AB\) and \(AC\), respectively. If \(DE=7\), find the length of \(BC\).
The side lengths of \(\triangle ABC\) are \(6\), \(8\), and \(10\). Points \(D\), \(E\), and \(F\) are the midpoints of the three sides, respectively. Find the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\).

Connecting the midpoints of consecutive sides of quadrilateral \(ABCD\) forms quadrilateral \(EFGH\). Given that the diagonals have lengths \(AC=8\) and \(BD=6\), find the perimeter of quadrilateral \(EFGH\).
Which of the following properties does a rectangle have that a general parallelogram does not necessarily have?

choices.A: Opposite sides are equal in length
choices.C: The diagonals are equal in length

displayedInputs.question: The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) of rectangle \(ABCD\) intersect at \(O\). Given \(\angle AOB=60^\circ\) and \(AC=8\), find the length of \(AB\).
In rectangle \(ABCD\), \(AB=6\) and \(BC=8\). The diagonals intersect at \(O\). Find the area of \(\triangle OAB\).
The diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) of rectangle \(ABCD\) intersect at \(O\). Also, \(AE\perp BD\) at \(E\), and \(\angle DAE=3\angle BAE\). Find the measure of \(\angle EAC\) in degrees.
In right triangle \(ABC\), the hypotenuse has length \(AB=10\). How long is the median \(CD\) to the hypotenuse? (Enter only the number.)
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), and the median \(CD\) to the hypotenuse \(AB\) has length \(6.5\). Find the length of \(AB\).
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), \(AC=6\), and \(BC=8\). Find the length of the median \(CD\) to the hypotenuse \(AB\).
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle C=90^\circ\), and \(CD\) is the median to the hypotenuse \(AB\). Given \(CD=5\) and \(AC=6\), find the area of \(\triangle ABC\).
